A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GoalRank study and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated content can be matched reliably. v1 explicitly defers its proof; this is a documented omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original offline comparisons, scaling experiments, group-size and reward-bias analyses, and online A/B results in Tables 1–4 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical studies and adds RankMixer comparisons and latency/MFU measurements in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: The reference-policy construction, optimization objective, reward-model training, and group-generation procedures are unchanged. Appendix D.2 newly describes a Transformer implementation, but neither version identifies this as an architectural revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use ML-1M, Amazon-Book, Industry, Industry-0.1B, and the same online short-video ranking task. The added comparisons and efficiency measurements introduce no distinct dataset, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: v2 adds RankMixer to the main benchmark comparison in Table 1 and the Industry-0.1B scaling comparison in Figure 3. All previous comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces evaluation using online latency and MFU. Existing data splits, retrieval procedures, list lengths, model-size ranges, and online traffic/duration protocols remain unchanged. The shared-evaluator statement newly documents a control rather than establishing a changed setting.

E4.justification: v2 adds an efficiency analysis comparing single-stage GoalRank with MG-E and extends the model-size sensitivity analysis to RankMixer. The group-size and reward-bias ablations in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report five independent offline runs, Student t-test significance at p < 0.05 for Table 1, and statistical significance for Table 4. No new seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds RankMixer results in Table 1 and Figure 3 while retaining earlier method scores. The stronger AUC comparator changes GoalRank's reported improvement from 7.98% to 5.59% on ML-1M and from 7.85% to 7.73% on Industry; GoalRank's scores are unchanged. Appendix D.3 newly reports GoalRank versus MG-E latency of 18.611 versus 34.235 ms and MFU of 12.65% versus 2.03%.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix B only promises a future proof. v2 Appendix A supplies masked-autoregressive definitions, compactness and dimension arguments, universal-approximation and KL bounds, a mixture-emulation proposition, and a detailed argument for Theorem 1. The new strict-gap result assumes bounded parameter domains and a dimension deficit, and applies to almost every fully supported target.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: generator-only approximation superiority and scaling, group-relative optimization, and superior offline/online performance. The headline theoretical claim is not narrowed to reflect the new appendix assumptions.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 newly attributes lower latency to eliminating evaluator scoring and multiple candidate-list constructions, and argues that parallel group generation and higher MFU avoid additional training cost. Existing reward-bias interpretations and limitations concerning changing business objectives are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the generator's Transformer feature-crossing block and autoregressive decoder, Top-1/sampling options, a shared reward model, and parallelizable group construction. The promised code-release destination changes from GitHub to an anonymous repository; both versions still describe future release rather than establish availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds RankMixer and universal-approximation references, including Cybenko, Hornik, Leshno, Sonoda and Murata, and Yun. The existing ranking-paradigm taxonomy and broad research positioning remain; relocating related work into Section 2 is primarily structural.

P1.justification: v2 merges and rewrites the preliminaries and former related-work appendix into Section 2, locally shortens experimental prose, renumbers appendices, and adds named Reproducibility and Ethics statements. Most existing main-text prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains a RankMixer row, and Figure 3 gains RankMixer curves with revised colors and legend. Figure 2 is relocated, and Figure 4 and Table 5 are repositioned without changing their content. The overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: RankMixer comparisons, a concrete generator description, and efficiency measurements improve evaluation and transparency. v2 also replaces the deferred proof with inspectable derivations. However, Appendix A's strict-gap argument requires additional assumptions and applies to almost every fully supported target, while Theorem 1 retains its unrestricted claim. The central theoretical deficiency is therefore only partly addressed, limiting the overall quality gain.
